questions.prompt: Two normal author rules in different cascade layers target an element. One has higher specificity but is in an earlier layer. What is considered first?

choices.text: Selector specificity is resolved first and always overrides layer ordering.
Document source order is resolved before layer priority and selector specificity.
Layer precedence is resolved before selector specificity.
An earlier layer wins normal declarations because its rules were registered first.

questions.explanation: The cascade compares origin, importance and layer order before specificity. Specificity only decides within the applicable precedence.

sources.title: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5
sources.claim: The cascade considers origin, importance and layers before specificity, and inheritance supplies inherited values when applicable.

questions.prompt: An inherited property has `unset` applied to a child. What does unset mean for that property?

choices.text: Use the initial value even though this property normally inherits.
Use the inherited value from the parent.
Revert to the value from a lower cascade origin rather than choosing inheritance.
Copy the most recent authored value rather than consulting property inheritance.

questions.explanation: Unset acts like inherit for inherited properties and initial for non-inherited properties. It does not change the DOM.

sources.title: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5
sources.claim: The cascade considers origin, importance and layers before specificity, and inheritance supplies inherited values when applicable.

questions.prompt: A flex row has a long unbreakable item that will not shrink as expected. Which rule is relevant before blaming flex-shrink?

choices.text: The automatic minimum main size can constrain how far it shrinks.
flex-shrink always forces the item below its automatic minimum size.
flex-basis:0 removes every content-based minimum without any min-size change.
justify-content controls minimum item width before the flex sizing algorithm.

questions.explanation: Automatic minimum sizes can keep a flex item at its content-based minimum. Shrink factors do not simply erase minimum-size constraints.

sources.title: CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1
sources.claim: Flex layout distributes space along a main axis, has automatic minimum sizes, and visual reordering does not change logical navigation order.

questions.prompt: A grid defines columns but auto-placement needs additional rows. Where do those rows come from?

choices.text: Only explicit row tracks exist, so additional items must overlap the last defined row.
grid-template-columns also determines the size of every automatically created row.
Every implicit track is sized by grid-template-rows even when no row is declared.
The implicit grid creates tracks controlled by auto-track sizing.

questions.explanation: Grid can create implicit tracks beyond the explicit grid. Auto-track sizing controls those generated tracks.

sources.title: CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1
sources.claim: Grid defines rows and columns, explicit and implicit tracks, fractional free-space distribution and auto-placement.

questions.prompt: A low-specificity important author declaration competes with a high-specificity normal author declaration. Which wins in this comparison?

choices.text: The high-specificity normal rule wins because specificity precedes importance.
The later normal rule wins because document order precedes importance.
The important declaration wins before specificity is compared.
The earlier important rule loses because important only breaks equal-specificity ties.

questions.explanation: Importance changes cascade priority, so a normal declaration cannot win this comparison solely through higher specificity.

questions.prompt: A non-inherited property has `unset` applied. What value selection does this request?

choices.text: Its parent computed value because unset makes every property inherit.
Its initial value rather than automatic inheritance from the parent.
A value from a lower cascade origin because unset always acts like revert.
A value from an earlier layer because unset always acts like revert-layer.

questions.explanation: Unset uses initial for a non-inherited property. It does not make all properties inherit.

sources.title: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5

questions.prompt: A CSS review compares conflicting rules. Which cascade claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Layer ordering can decide between normal author rules.
Specificity decides every conflict across all origins.
Source order overrides origin and importance whenever a rule appears later.
An ID selector always defeats normal declarations in a higher-priority layer.
Importance is considered before specificity.

questions.explanation: a: Layer priority precedes specificity. b: Origins and importance can take priority over specificity. c: Source order is a later tie-breaker, not a replacement for higher-priority criteria. d: ID specificity is considered after applicable layer priority. e: The cascade separates important and normal priorities first.

sources.title: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5

questions.prompt: A component uses CSS-wide keywords. Which meanings hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: unset behaves like inherit on inherited properties.
unset acts like inherit even for non-inherited properties.
initial restores the element user-agent stylesheet value in every case.
inherit requests the parent computed value.
initial requests the property initial value.

questions.explanation: a: Its behavior follows whether the property inherits. b: Unset acts like initial for non-inherited properties. c: It requests the property initial value, which need not be the element default stylesheet value. d: Inheritance explicitly selects that parent value. e: It is not necessarily the browser default style of that element.

questions.prompt: A Flex layout must preserve usability. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Changing order updates both visual positions and the DOM reading sequence.
flex-shrink ignores every explicit minimum-size constraint.
flex-direction establishes the main axis.
Automatic minimum sizes can limit item shrinking.
order changes the logical screen-reader reading order.

questions.explanation: a: Flex order changes visual order without changing source order. b: Minimum constraints participate in the sizing algorithm. c: The main-axis direction follows this property. d: Minimum-size constraints still apply during flex sizing. e: Visual reordering does not change source order.

sources.claim: Flex layout distributes space along a main axis, has automatic minimum sizes, and visual reordering does not change logical navigation order.

questions.prompt: A grid contains explicit and automatically placed items. Which track claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Every fr track is a fixed pixel length in all containers.
Grid defines rows and columns for two-dimensional layout.
Auto-placement can create implicit tracks.
Each fr unit is the same as one equal percentage of the full container width.
grid-template-columns controls the size of every automatically generated row.

questions.explanation: a: Its size depends on flexible space allocation. b: Items are laid out against the grid axes. c: Items can require tracks beyond the explicit grid. d: Flexible sizing distributes leftover space after other track constraints, not a fixed percentage of the full width. e: Rows use their applicable row track-sizing rules, not the explicit column sizes.
